The truth is, my opinion is divided because I received both excellent and VERY BAD service on the same day.

First, a very friendly girl helped us by checking the price of a litter box. When we left, I had three bags of pet food, a total of 20 kg, and to carry my shopping, I used her cart. When I went back to return it, another saleswoman (brunette, shoulder-length straight hair) told me I couldn't take the cart out. I apologized and explained the situation, and she said, "I don't care, it's not allowed."
She started mocking me, pointing to the sign they have that says you CAN'T bring in carts that don't belong to the store. I told her that it didn't say what she was saying, but that I had returned the cart anyway (it only took three minutes).

In conclusion: she was extremely unpleasant and rude. It doesn't take much to be polite. Especially considering it was out of necessity.

I should have filed a complaint, but it fell on deaf ears.

A terrible experience at Kiwoko. We bought two rabbits separately just two days ago. One seemed healthy, but the other started feeling very ill from the moment we left the store. It arrived home with the entire box full of diarrhea, and in less than 24 hours we had to rush it to the vet. It received a critical diagnosis, as it wasn't eating and it was clear it hadn't drunk water in over 24 hours. The vet obviously gave us instructions on how to prevent the other rabbit from catching anything my rabbit might have, and told us to change everything it had been wearing the day before—NEW, RECENTLY PURCHASED—meaning more expenses.

The subsequent handling of the situation has been even worse. To begin with, when I went to the store yesterday and explained the whole ordeal, the woman told me that the two rabbits we bought (because we adopted two) were checked before being put in the boxes, which is completely false. The guy just put them in the box as soon as he picked them up. Instead of offering real solutions, they told us they had to "assess" the rabbit's case before making a change, since a same-day exchange wasn't possible. They didn't refund my money or anything; I waited almost an hour because I obviously felt scammed. They had to call the manager to come up with a solution, which was to give us the same kit we bought for the other rabbit. I have no complaints about that, but I do complain about all the complaining I had to do to get any kind of solution. Otherwise, I would have gone home empty-handed, waiting for them to review the case after selling us a sick animal.

Furthermore, neither rabbit has a veterinary record, which we find completely irresponsible for animals sold in a specialized store.

To top it all off, they made us sign a supposed purchase contract that's nowhere to be found. They won't let us download it, they won't give us a copy, and we still don't have access to a document that, in theory, we signed. When we entered our Gmail address, which we know perfectly well because it's our work tool, it told both of us that the PIN was incorrect. I mentioned it at the store, and they said it was very strange, but we didn't get a solution.

A complete lack of transparency, empathy, and responsibility. We're talking about living beings, not merchandise. An absolutely terrible experience.

This comment isn't directed at this specific store, but rather at Kiwoko online for their poor shipping management. I placed an order, specifying my address and requesting a delivery time at the collection point, as they would be closed otherwise. They tried to deliver it to me twice outside their designated area. I opened a support ticket because they told me they were returning the package, and I reminded them about the delivery time and asked them to leave it at a collection point. They finally told me it was resolved, but then tried to deliver the package again at 8:30 PM. We had the same argument, and they ended up leaving it at an unauthorized collection point, which they charged me 50 cents for pickup—completely unreasonable since shipping was already included. Their logistics are appalling.
